{
"Microservice": "A small, independently deployable service that implements a specific business capability and owns its data within a microservices architecture.",
"Service": "A software component that performs a specific function and exposes its capabilities to other components through a well-defined interface.",
"API": "An Application Programming Interface that defines the contract through which software components interact, specifying available operations and data formats.",
"APIGateway": "A server that acts as a single entry point into a microservices system, routing client requests to appropriate backend services and handling cross-cutting concerns like authentication and rate limiting.",
"REST": "An architectural style for synchronous communication over HTTP that uses standard methods and resource-based URIs to exchange data between services.",
"gRPC": "A high-performance, synchronous remote procedure call framework that uses HTTP/2 and Protocol Buffers for efficient inter-service communication.",
"Event": "A message representing a significant occurrence or state change within a system, typically published asynchronously for other services to consume.",
"EventBus": "A messaging infrastructure that facilitates asynchronous communication between services by routing events from publishers to interested subscribers.",
"ServiceMesh": "A dedicated infrastructure layer that manages inter-service communication, providing capabilities such as traffic routing, observability, and security between microservices.",
"CircuitBreaker": "A resilience pattern that monitors service calls and stops forwarding requests to a failing service to prevent cascading failures and allow recovery.",
"SynchronousCommunication": "An interaction pattern in which the caller blocks and waits for an immediate response from the called service, typically used in REST and gRPC calls.",
"AsynchronousCommunication": "An interaction pattern in which the sender does not wait for an immediate response, typically achieved through events and message queues.",
"CascadingFailure": "A failure scenario in which the failure of one service triggers successive failures in dependent services, potentially bringing down an entire system.",
"MicroservicesArchitecture": "An architectural style that structures an application as a collection of small, loosely coupled, independently deployable services, each owning its own data and business capability.",
"InterServiceCommunication": "The exchange of messages and data between services within a distributed system, which can be synchronous or asynchronous in nature.",
"LooseCoupling": "A design property in which services have minimal dependencies on one another, allowing them to evolve, scale, and fail independently.",
"IndependentlyDeployableService": "A service that can be built, tested, and released to production on its own schedule without requiring coordinated deployment of other services.",
"DataOwnership": "The principle that each microservice exclusively manages its own data store, ensuring that other services access its data only through its APIs."
}
